lead.headline: October CPI Rises 0.4%, Hotter Than Expected
lead.summary: The consumer price index rose a seasonally adjusted 0.4% in October, more than economists expected, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Tuesday. Core inflation rose 0.3%.

tech.headline: Anthropic Launches Claude Meetings to Turn Discussions Into Plans and Tasks
tech.summary: Anthropic launched Claude Meetings, a feature that converts workplace discussions into plans and tasks.

tech.headline: Adobe Adds AI Agents and an MCP to Photoshop, Premiere and Firefly
tech.summary: Adobe is releasing a local MCP to expose more Creative Cloud features to AI agents. It also added new creative tools across its apps.

tech.headline: Reddit Turns User Conversations Into AI-Powered Product Reviews
tech.summary: Reddit's new AI reviews summarize what users like and dislike about 10,000 products. The feature targets holiday shoppers.

business.headline: Bond Yields Surge Most in 19 Months as Traders Brace for Fed Hikes
business.summary: Treasury yields jumped after the hot inflation reading. Traders priced in a 91% chance of a quarter-point Fed hike in December and a 9% chance of a half-point hike, per CME FedWatch.

business.headline: Nvidia Sells Off for a Second Day Over Huang Fallout
business.summary: Nvidia shares sank 5.47% Tuesday as investors weighed the fallout from CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy. The stock had already fallen about 4% Monday.

world.headline: House GOP Leaders Block Vote on Hegseth Impeachment Push
world.summary: House Republican leaders killed an effort to force a vote on impeaching Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Rep. Thomas Massie's articles accuse Hegseth of waging the Iran war without congressional approval and ignoring laws meant to minimize civilian casualties.

world.headline: Trump Says Renewed Strikes on Iran Are 'Quite Unlikely'
world.summary: President Trump said Monday that a renewed military campaign against Iran is quite unlikely and does not seem necessary. He tied that to progress in negotiations over Iran's nuclear program.

world.headline: Israeli Strikes and Gunfire Kill Four in Gaza
world.summary: Hospital authorities said Israeli strikes and gunfire killed four people in the Gaza Strip on Tuesday. Three of the deaths came in two separate incidents.

opinion.headline: The Nvidia Spy Scandal Was Hiding in Plain Sight
opinion.summary: Ignatius argues that Jensen Huang appears to be the most prominent American yet caught in a Chinese intelligence honey trap. He says the evidence suggests China's spy service was running both a chip supply-chain operation and an influence operation on U.S. tech policy. He argues that Washington was slow to see the risk.
opinion.author: David Ignatius

opinion.headline: Did a Blue Tsunami Just End an Era? Not So Fast
opinion.summary: Ferguson argues that the 2026 midterms were a regular shellacking rather than a political paradigm shift. He draws on history, from Eisenhower to Nixon, to show what tends to happen when a second term turns sour.
opinion.author: Niall Ferguson

opinion.headline: Kevin Warsh Is Now Free to Unleash His Inner Hawk
opinion.summary: Levin argues that after the hotter-than-expected October consumer price report, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh should raise interest rates again at the next meeting. He says inflation is running around 3.9% against a 2% goal, and that even another hike may not be enough to tame it.
opinion.author: Jonathan Levin

sports.headline: Celtics Rout 76ers 123-101 as Tatum Outduels Jaylen Brown
sports.summary: Jayson Tatum scored 21 points and Paul George had 36 as the Celtics beat Philadelphia 123-101 on Tuesday. It was the first meeting with former teammate Jaylen Brown.

sports.headline: Patriots' Injury Run Gets Worse Ahead of Munich Game
sports.summary: The Patriots are missing Will Campbell and Ben Brown, among others, with knee injuries, plus further hamstring problems. The injuries follow a 45-27 home loss to Green Bay.
